append_evidence.source_title: VTKD Rule Book Archive — WT Virtual Taekwondo Rules and Regulations (April 2026)
append_evidence.limitations: Provider-hosted rules archive. It documents official event setup but does not establish geographically separated synchronous competition.
First-party operational documentation. Same-network and Game Master setup support the examined event architecture, not every possible deployment.
Patch notes document calibration and match-system changes but do not provide a remote latency or multi-site integrity specification.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: The examined official competition and setup materials describe players at event stations joined through a shared Game Master and local network architecture.
distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Shared match room and Game Master within the documented event setup.
distributed_arena_relation.latency_governance: No public specification examined establishes latency budgets or remediation for geographically separated synchronous opponents.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Event calibration procedures are documented; cross-site equivalence is not established.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Software, referees, and event operators administer one shared match state.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Local mat, boundary, display, and calibration requirements are documented; remote-site safety equivalence is not.
distributed_arena_relation.uncertainty: This conclusion is limited to examined public materials. A private or future remote mode may exist without being evidenced here.

agency_segments.boundary_description: A permitted task-execution regime in which pilot input directly controls the exoskeleton.
agency_segments.transition_trigger: Team- and device-specific; public discipline material does not identify an observed transition sequence.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Manual exoskeleton operation and permitted sensing/actuation.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Pilot performance is primary while the device mediates and amplifies execution.
agency_segments.uncertainty: This is a permitted regime, not proof that every team used it or used it for a specific task.

agency_segments.boundary_description: A permitted regime in which pilot input and automated control jointly determine task execution.
agency_segments.transition_trigger: Input device, intention detection, or device logic depending on implementation.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Shared and not resolvable without task-level control logs.
agency_segments.uncertainty: Public sources do not expose per-team mode transitions or causal percentages.

agency_segments.boundary_description: A permitted regime in which autonomous device functions may execute part of a task.
agency_segments.transition_trigger: Device-specific automated mode or detected state.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Autonomous operation is explicitly permitted by the discipline description.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Automation may become primary for the segment; pilot contribution before, after, or through triggering remains implementation-specific.
agency_segments.uncertainty: The source establishes permission, not the exact autonomous behavior of each team.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: The classified EXO contest is evaluated as a physical task course, not a distributed shared arena.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Device-specific control and assistance remain relevant to comparability, but not as a distributed-arena relation.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Officials evaluate task completion and time on the physical course.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Pilot, assistive device, and course safety are local and constitutive.

append_evidence.limitations: Official task description establishes command timing and animated task structure, not a general philosophical definition of athletic embodiment.

agency_segments.phase_or_regime: intentional command generation and decoder-mediated execution
agency_segments.boundary_description: Each command opportunity or continuous-control interval in the animated race.
agency_segments.transition_trigger: Task prompt, pilot-generated brain activity, and decoder classification.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Participant-specific signal acquisition, calibration, and decoding.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Human intention is causally necessary, while the decoder mediates whether and how it becomes a valid command.
agency_segments.uncertainty: Decoder performance and participant-specific calibration materially affect attribution and comparability.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: The examined BCI race uses a computational task environment and does not depend on geographically distributed opponents.
distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Common task software and event timing.
distributed_arena_relation.latency_governance: Decoder latency is a performance and measurement issue, not a multi-site network relation in this case.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Participant-specific calibration is material and remains only partially comparable.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Software and officials determine task completion and ranking.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Participant fatigue and signal burden are local human limits.

intentional_biological_control.summary: The pilot intentionally generates brain-activity patterns that are decoded into task commands. This establishes a live bodily-origin performance channel but does not by itself settle Spatial Athletic System membership.
intentional_biological_control.uncertainty: The boundary between intentional physiological performance and athletic embodiment remains theoretical and participant-specific.

agency_segments.boundary_description: Before the timed course run, teams design, program, configure, and test the robotic system.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: All eligible pre-run engineering within challenge rules.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Human design contribution is substantial but occurs outside the live course-execution segment.
agency_segments.uncertainty: The public overview does not expose every configuration action or team workflow.

agency_segments.boundary_description: During the timed run, human operators supervise systems from the command post and may issue permitted commands.
agency_segments.transition_trigger: Operator intervention, communications state, or autonomous system behavior.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Supervision and permitted command interaction under event rules.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Human contribution is live but may be intermittent; exact causal allocation requires command logs.
agency_segments.uncertainty: The examined sources do not provide a universal per-team intervention timeline.

agency_segments.boundary_description: Robots map, navigate, search, and report within the subterranean course during autonomous operation.
agency_segments.transition_trigger: Autonomous mission execution and loss or restoration of operator intervention.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: Autonomy, perception, networking, and robot coordination permitted by the challenge.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Autonomous system performance is primary in the course; human design remains an upstream cause.
agency_segments.uncertainty: Systems teams differed in autonomy and intervention patterns.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: Human supervisors occupy a command post while robots perform in a separate hazardous physical course.
distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Robot telemetry, maps, networking, and command systems connect the command post to the course.
distributed_arena_relation.latency_governance: Communications degradation is part of the technical challenge rather than a normalized athlete-to-athlete fairness condition.
distributed_arena_relation.calibration_equivalence: Not intended as identical-system calibration; heterogeneous systems are compared through common tasks and scoring.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: DARPA validates spatial reports, timing, and ranking from the shared competition infrastructure.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Physical separation reduces direct human exposure while robot and course safety remain governed.
distributed_arena_relation.uncertainty: This is distributed supervision, not a remote human-versus-human athletic arena.

agency_segments.boundary_description: The rule-defined voting process allocates an optional power resource to selected drivers.
agency_segments.transition_trigger: Completion of the official vote and award of the resource.
agency_segments.allowed_assistance: The awarded boost is permitted by the historical championship rule.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Spectators affect available resources but do not execute vehicle performance.
agency_segments.uncertainty: The source does not quantify the resource's causal effect on any specific result.

agency_segments.boundary_description: During the race, the driver decides whether and when to deploy the awarded boost while retaining vehicle control.
agency_segments.transition_trigger: Driver deployment decision under the rule.
agency_segments.causal_attribution: Driver execution remains the live performance channel; the spectator contribution is upstream and indirect.
agency_segments.uncertainty: Competitive effect varies by race context and is not quantified here.

distributed_arena_relation.physical_site_relation: The race is a physical circuit contest; fan voting occurs externally and does not create a distributed performance arena.
distributed_arena_relation.synchronization_mechanism: Voting and vehicle systems communicate resource eligibility and deployment.
distributed_arena_relation.officiation_relation: Officials and vehicle systems administer eligibility and deployment under the rule.
distributed_arena_relation.safety_relation: Motorsport safety remains separate from the voting mechanism.

participatory_actor_relations.action_window: Official FANBOOST voting period before resource deployment.
participatory_actor_relations.mechanism: Public votes determine which eligible drivers receive an optional power resource.
participatory_actor_relations.resource_or_constraint_effect: Allocates an optional rule-authorized power resource; the driver retains deployment and driving control.
participatory_actor_relations.uncertainty: The effect on a specific race result is not quantified.
